title: Stripes or Spots? Animal Patterns for Kids with Milo
description:
Stripes or spots? Look closely with Milo the bluebird and pick your answer! Then look even closer: a zebra's skin is black under its stripes, a tiger's skin is striped too, a baby panda is born pink and as small as a stick of butter, and every cow's spots are like a fingerprint.
An interactive look-and-find animal lesson for kids ages 2-6, with questions to answer, counting, actions to copy and a quiz at the end.
facts: Zebras have black skin underneath their striped coat (Britannica; San Diego Zoo).
A tiger's stripes are also on its skin, and no two tigers have the same stripes (WWF).
A newborn giant panda is pink, almost hairless and about the size of a stick of butter; the black and white markings appear within a few weeks (Smithsonian's National Zoo; National Geographic).
The black and white pattern of every Holstein cow is unique, like a fingerprint (Holstein Association USA).

segments.name: hello
lines: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today we are looking for patterns!
Stripes are long lines. Like the lines on a stripy sock.
Spots are round dots. Like the dots on a spotty ball.
Some animal friends wear stripes. Some wear spots.
Put on your looking eyes. Are you ready? Let's go!

segments.name: zebra
lines: Look at this friend.
Stripes! Black and white stripes. It is the zebra!
close:zebra

lines.t: Now look closer. What color is a zebra's skin, under all that hair?

lines: Here is the fun fact. Under the stripes, a zebra's skin is black!
exhibit
Black skin, with black and white hair growing on top.
exhibit
And every zebra has its own stripes. No two zebras match!
close:zebra
A baby zebra knows its mama by her stripes.
Say it with me. Zebra skin is black!
close:host
Can you draw stripes in the air? Down, down, down!
Super stripes!

short.title: A Zebra's Skin Is Black Under Its Stripes!

segments.name: tiger
lines: Here comes an orange friend.
Stripes! Orange and black stripes. It is the tiger!
close:tiger

lines.t: Are the stripes only on the fur?

lines: No! Here is the fun fact. A tiger's skin is stripy too!
exhibit
Stripes on the fur, and the very same stripes on the skin underneath.
exhibit
And no two tigers have the same stripes.
close:tiger
Say it with me. Tiger skin is stripy too!
close:host
Can you creep like a tiger? Creep, creep, creep. Pounce!
What a quiet tiger!

short.title: A Tiger's Skin Is Stripy Too! Stripes or Spots?

segments.name: panda
lines: Look at this round friend, with black and white patches. It is the panda!

lines.t: Now, what color is a newborn baby panda? Black and white? Or pink?

lines: Pink! Here is the fun fact. A baby panda is born pink!
Look how tiny! A newborn panda is as small as a stick of butter.
exhibit
The black and white patches grow later, when the baby is a few weeks old.
close:cub
A grown-up panda is big. But its baby is one of the tiniest babies of all!
exhibit
The mama panda holds her tiny baby very, very gently.
Say it with me. Baby pandas are born pink!
close:host
Can you curl up small like a baby panda? Tiny, tiny, tiny!
So tiny and cute!

short.title: Baby Pandas Are Born Pink! As Small as Butter

segments.name: cow
lines: Moo! Look at this farm friend.
Spots! Big black spots. It is the cow!
close:cow

lines.t: Do any two cows have the same spots?

lines: No! Here is the fun fact. Every spotted cow has her very own spots.
Her spots are like your fingerprint. Nobody else has the same one!
exhibit
Let's count some spots. One spot, two spots, three spots!
exhibit
Say it with me. Every cow has her own spots!
close:host
Can you draw a spot in the air? Round and round!
Beautiful spots!

short.title: Every Cow Has Her Own Spots, Like a Fingerprint!

segments.name: quiz
lines: Wow! We found so many patterns. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
quiz: Whose skin is black under the stripes?
Who is born pink, and as small as a stick of butter?
Whose spots are like a fingerprint?

segments.name: goodbye
lines: You learned four new things today.
Stripes on the zebra. Stripes on the tiger. Patches on the panda. And spots on the cow!
Can you find stripes or spots at home today? Maybe on a sock. Maybe on a ball!
Thank you for looking with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
